questions.text: A record containing Ghidra pseudocode has confidence observed. What does that observation establish?

options.A: The function executed and produced every result suggested by the text.
options.B: The recovered signature exactly matches the original source signature.
options.C: The provider emitted that text; its behavioral meaning still needs analysis.
options.D: The function has no unresolved behavior because the record is observed.

questions.explanation: The observation is of the provider output. Interpreting its meaning is a derivation, and predicting execution is an inference until supported by appropriate runs.

questions.text: A claim covers grade(score) for all eleven scores from 90 through 100. Agreeing observed runs exist only for 95 and 100. How should the lesson’s ledger classify the claim?

options.A: pass, because both tested inputs agree with the prediction.
options.B: unknown, because nine claimed inputs have no observed run.
options.C: fail, because every untested input counts as a disagreement.
options.D: unsupported, because no input has an observed run.

questions.explanation: Partial coverage with no disagreement is unknown: 2 of 11 inputs are covered. No observations would be unsupported; any disagreement would be fail.

questions.text: c_div computes quotient = abs(a) // abs(b), then returns quotient for matching signs and -quotient otherwise. What is c_div(1000, -7)?
questions.explanation: The absolute quotient is 142. Opposite signs negate it to -142, implementing truncation toward zero rather than Python’s floor division.
